'''Scott Dodelson''' is an American physicist. He is a professor of physics at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] and chair of its physics department.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=University |first=Carnegie Mellon |title=Scott Dodelson - Department of Physics - Carnegie Mellon University |url=http://www.cmu.edu/physics/people/faculty/dodelson.html |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=www.cmu.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Dodelson received his B.A., B.S., and Ph.D. from [[Columbia University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Department of Astronomy & Astrophysics - Profile: Scott Dodelson |url=https://lambda.gsfc.nasa.gov/product/suborbit/DASI/astro.uchicago.edu/people/scott-dodelson.shtml.html |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=lambda.gsfc.nasa.gov }}{{Dead link|date=November 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> His thesis supervisor was [[Gerald Feinberg]]. He was a research fellow at Harvard University before moving to the [[Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]]. He joined the [[University of Chicago]] faculty in 1998 and was professor until 2017, when he joined Carnegie Mellon University.<ref name=":0" /> His research has focused on the intersection of physics and [[cosmology]] and has out studies on [[dark matter]], [[dark energy]], and cosmological neutrinos.<ref>{{Cite web |last=University |first=Carnegie Mellon |date=August 15, 2017 |title=Scott Dodelson Appointed Head of Carnegie Mellon's Department of Physics - News - Carnegie Mellon University |url=http://www.cmu.edu/news/stories/archives/2017/august/dodelson-appointed-physics-head.html |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=www.cmu.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Scott Dodelson seeks collaboration as head of the Department of Physics - The Tartan |url=http://thetartan.org/2017/9/11/news/physics |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=thetartan.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Overbye |first=Dennis |date=2019-02-25 |title=Have Dark Forces Been Messing With the Cosmos? |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/02/25/science/cosmos-hubble-dark-energy.html |access-date=2022-06-14 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> He has played a key role in numerous cosmological surveys, including co-chairing the Science Committee of the [[Dark Energy Survey]].<ref name=":0" />

From 2006 to 2008, Dodelson was interim director of the [[Fermilab Center for Particle Astrophysics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fermilab Today |url=https://www.fnal.gov/pub/today/archive/archive_2007/today07-09-26.html |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=www.fnal.gov}}</ref> He was head of Fermilab's Theoretical Astrophysics Group from 2001 to 2006.<ref name=":0" />

Dodelson is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]. He was managing editor of [[International Journal of Modern Physics|International Journal of Modern Physics D]] from 2004 to 2008. He is the author of the astrophysics textbook ''Modern Cosmology''.<ref name=":0" /> The minor planet [[148707 Dodelson]] is named after him.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Schmadel |first=Lutz D. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dzBsCQAAQBAJ&dq=148707+Dodelson&pg=PA204 |title=Dictionary of Minor Planet Names: Addendum to 6th Edition: 2012-2014 |date=2015-05-14 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-319-17677-2 |language=en}}</ref>
